executive_summary: USD/SGD stood at 1.2793 on the payload spot date of 2026-10-02. The pair is quoted in Singapore dollars per US dollar, so a rising number means a stronger dollar. Over one month the pair is up 0.96%, as the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike pulled it off its early-September low. It is down 1.03% over three months, up 0.50% over six months and down 1.29% over a year. On a closing basis it sits at the 38th percentile of its 52-week range (1.26139–1.30791). The main bilateral story is a contest between two forces. On the dollar side there is roughly 195.5bp of carry against the Singapore 6-month T-bill proxy, plus fresh speculative dollar buying. On the Singapore side there is the widest growth gap in the set (5.9% vs 2.1%), a current-account gap of about 19.6pp of GDP, and a MAS band that appreciates every day whatever the dollar does. The bilateral view differs from the two standalone dossiers. The USD dossier is Bullish tactically at +0.3782, but that falls to a marginal +0.1024 against SGD, because SGD is not a funding currency being sold into dollar strength: it has its own hawkish central bank and its own haven bid. The settled verdict is Bullish tactically (conviction 2, net score +0.1024) and Bearish strategically (conviction 3, net score −0.3540). Treat them as two steps in sequence: collect carry into the low part of the seven-touch 1.2812–1.29395 resistance band, then build the strategic short from there. The main caveat is new since pass 1. The MAS Advance Release Calendar puts the October statement no later than 14 Oct 2026, not in the last week of October as the verdict assumed. OCBC now expects Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to slightly steepen the S$ Nominal Effective Exchange Rate Index (S$NEER) slope at the mid-October meeting. Standard Chartered calls the same move but notes that "This may be a close call, with a pause as the main risk." My own view is that the tactical Bullish call is more fragile than its score shows: the event most likely to overturn it now lands inside the first two weeks of the window, on the same day as US CPI. The verdict stands as issued.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Both dossiers' REER-relative proxies agree that SGD is rich against the dollar. The SGD dossier puts USD/SGD fair value near 1.3750 (SGD about 7.6% rich). The USD dossier puts it near 1.3778 (USD about 7.1% cheap against SGD). The SGD BIS REER of 114.81 sits at the 75th percentile of its post-2024 range and is the second-richest in G10+SGD. The USD REER of 106.70 sits at only the 9th percentile of its own recent range. The richness is policy-sanctioned, not a mispricing waiting to correct: MAS manages the nominal effective rate, and its band has appreciated for two decades. Spot therefore prices Singapore's productivity premium and the appreciating band, but not a flatter band. Valuation is not a mean-reversion signal for this pair over either horizon.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Annualised carry is +195.5bp to a long USD/SGD position, using the Fed's 3.875% effective midpoint against the 1.92% 6-month SGS T-bill proxy (24 September auction); it is 208bp on the 4.00% upper bound. On 3-month compounded SORA (1.06% Q2 average) it would be about 281bp, a basis uncertainty of roughly 86bp that comes from Singapore having no policy rate. The framework's carry-to-vol ratio is null because no implied vol exists; as a realised-vol proxy only, carry / 60-day realised vol is 1.955 / 3.17 ≈ +0.62 and carry / 20-day realised ≈ +0.66, flattered by very low realised vol and not the same statistic as the framework's. Carry worked over one month (pair +0.96% on top of about 21 pips of accrual) but failed over three months (pair −1.03%, more than the roughly 62 pips of accrual). In this pair, carry pays only when the dollar leg is gaining rate momentum; when momentum stalls, the band slope and SGD's haven bid overwhelm it.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Tactical weight raised from 0.24 to 0.26: the bilateral short-rate gap of about 195.5bp sits at the edge of the high-carry threshold, and because the quote leg has no policy rate the entire policy question reduces to one observable rate curve plus an unobservable band slope — there is no second OIS path for other factors to arbitrate, so rates carry proportionally more signal on this pair. Strategic at default.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: There is no bilateral policy-rate differential in the normal sense: the direction payload returns policyDifferential null because MAS targets the S$NEER band and publishes no policy rate. The usable proxy is the 6-month SGS T-bill cut-off of 1.92% at the 24 September auction against the Fed's 3.875% effective midpoint, a gap of about 195.5bp in the dollar's favour, or 208bp on the 4.00% upper bound. At ten years the gap is wider still, roughly 275bp (UST 5.24% against SGS near 2.49%), and it widened in September as the Treasury 10-year rose 45bp while SGS rose only 7bp. The transmission is direct and mechanical: a long USD/SGD position is paid that gap, and covered interest parity puts the forward curve at about a 1.96% annualised discount, so the carry and the forward are two views of the same number. Direction of travel over four weeks is close to flat. The Fed's only scheduled decision in the window, 2026-10-28, carries no projection round in the gated file, and October hike odds fell below a coin flip after Williams said on 2026-09-29 that there is no urgency; MAS's October statement is a genuine binary that the MAS survey prices near 45%, with CIMB expecting a steepening to about 1.50% and UOB expecting a hold at about 1.25% on softer core prints and a looser labour market. With both legs likely static, the positive carry is what is left, and it accrues to the pair rising.

tactical.what_is_priced: The forward curve already prices the whole 195.5bp gap as USD/SGD depreciation, and the MAS survey prices the October tightening at about 45% against our 40%. strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the level of the gap matters less than its direction, and the direction is mildly against the pair while the pricing of it is already rich. The Fed's September dots put the funds rate at 4.1% at end-2026 and end-2027, so the base leg is within one 25bp move of a plateau; the 2026-12-09 FOMC carries an SEP in the gated file and is the decision that either delivers that last hike or prices it out. On the quote leg, MAS has no scheduled decision on file and no policy rate to move, but its instrument appreciates by construction: a 1.25% slope lifts the S$NEER roughly 0.6% over six months whatever the dollar does, and Singapore short rates are rising with global yields, narrowing the proxy gap from the SGD side without MAS acting. That is a slow compression of about 25-50bp over the horizon. Against it, the forward already embeds 1.96% a year of pair decline, which is more than the band slope delivers against the basket, so a short-USD/SGD position has to beat the forward, not merely beat spot. The two effects are close to offsetting and neither side has an OIS path to disagree with. A Fed that stops at 4.00% while SGS yields keep rising would tip this Bearish; a December hike with a higher 2027 dot would tip it Bullish.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth differential is the widest on this pair of any G10 bilateral and it runs against the base. Singapore grew 5.9% year on year in Q2 2026 with first-half growth of 6.1%, and the government raised its 2026 forecast to 4.5-5.5% from 2.0-4.0%; the United States grew 2.1% year on year with Q2 revised to 2.2% annualised. The gap is roughly 3.8 percentage points. The surprise history is also asymmetric: August non-oil domestic exports rose 46.2% against a 35% consensus, the fastest since 1988, with electronics up 131.8%, while of 141 US releases with a forecast in September 60 beat and 65 missed, so US data are strong in level but balanced in surprise. On inflation the differential runs the other way in level — US headline 3.4% and core PCE 3.0% against Singapore headline 2.3% and MAS core 2.2% — but the trajectories invert it: US core PCE eased from 3.3% to 3.0% and core CPI sits at 2.4%, while MAS core is rising and at a two-year high in the upper half of MAS's 1.5-2.5% range. The transmission to this pair is indirect on the quote side, because Singapore's data move the exchange rate only through MAS's band rather than through a policy rate, which is why confidence is held at 52 rather than higher. The Singapore release calendar inside the window — Q3 advance GDP, September NODX and September CPI — is more likely to surprise strong than the US calendar.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the growth gap persists even as both economies decelerate at the margin. Enterprise Singapore lifted its 2026 NODX forecast to 14-16% from 3-5%, the MAS survey sees 2027 growth of 3.1% — still near potential — and MAS expects a positive output gap to widen slightly in 2026, which is the configuration that keeps a central bank biased to tighten. On the base leg the Fed's own projections have headline PCE falling from 3.7% in 2026 to 2.3% in 2027 and core PCE from 3.4% to 2.5% with unemployment flat at 4.1%: a soft landing, not an overheating economy, and US core measures are already running below the SEP's year-end core-PCE path. US household strain is visible in a 4.1% saving rate, Conference Board confidence at 81.9 and GDPNow falling from 5.1% to 3.7% in a fortnight. So the strategic picture is a decelerating base economy against a quote economy at the top of a capex cycle with rising core inflation, which argues for the pair to fall. The qualification, and the reason confidence is only 55, is concentration: Singapore's surge is one AI-driven electronics cycle, retrenchments at 4,620 are the highest since 4Q20, and UOB's recent read flags rising labour-market slack. A memory-cycle turn would remove the growth and the inflation support within two quarters and flip this factor.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a low-risk-sensitivity pair in the framework's taxonomy, and the current regime confirms it. The dollar sits on the right-hand side of its smile — US exceptionalism with a 10-year TIPS yield of 2.88% — and has a measured 60-day correlation with the S&P 500 of -0.31, so a genuine risk-off episode lifts the pair. But the Singapore dollar is itself a regional haven: it is one of the few Asian currencies to have appreciated through the Iran conflict, the sovereign is AAA with S$550.73bn of reserves, and in a China-specific or Asia-specific shock capital moves toward Singapore rather than away. The two haven bids partially cancel, which is why the pair's realised volatility of about 3.15% is the lowest in the G10+SGD set and roughly half that of AUD/USD. The current cross-asset split is itself two-sided: equities are complacent with the VIX at 16.39 at the 34th percentile and the S&P 500 at 7,666, while credit has repriced with US high-yield spreads 59bp wider in a month to 324bp, the 98th percentile of the year, and investment grade at 86bp. Credit stress is marginally base-positive; the Straits Times Index at a record and China's manufacturing PMI back at 50.1 are marginally quote-positive. Neither dominates over four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the two scenarios that would move this pair through the risk channel point in opposite directions and have similar probabilities. An AI-equity correction would hurt the quote leg twice over — it is Singapore's export engine and the source of the regional wealth-management inflows that underpin the currency — and would simultaneously push capital toward the dollar, so the pair would rise meaningfully. A Gulf settlement that removes the energy premium would do the reverse: it would lower Singapore's import bill, cut US headline inflation and the Fed's justification for a terminal hike, and move the dollar toward the bottom of its smile, so the pair would fall. A funding-stress episode in which high-yield spreads break beyond 450bp would push the dollar to the left of the smile and lift the pair hard, but that tail is small. Because the quote currency is a haven within its own region and the base currency is the global haven, the distribution is genuinely two-sided rather than skewed, and the pair's 3.15% realised volatility means even a sizeable shock produces a one-to-three percent move rather than the five-to-ten percent a high-beta cross would show. Neutral is the honest answer rather than a placeholder.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Positioning on the two legs is measured by entirely different instruments and currently points the same way for the pair. On the base leg, IMM speculators rebuilt their aggregate dollar long by $12.5bn to $18.4bn in the week to 2026-09-22, the fastest weekly increase in seven years, flipping leveraged funds from 21,041 contracts net short the dollar to 10,624 net long; StoneX puts the DXY-equivalent long at $17.3bn. That position is fresh rather than crowded — the combined leveraged-plus-asset-manager measure sits at the 44th percentile of its cached range — so there is room for it to grow before it becomes a squeeze risk. On the quote leg there is no CFTC contract at all, so positioning must be read from the policy instrument: bank estimates put the S$NEER 1.68-1.9% above its model mid-point in late July, with UOB confirming on 31 August that it remained above mid, and against an assumed band half-width near 2% that leaves very little headroom. MAS is visibly absorbing the inflow — official reserves rose S$1.43bn in August and S$48.71bn over the year to S$550.73bn — which is the mechanism by which good Singapore news stops reaching the exchange rate. Momentum in dollar flows plus a quote currency pinned against its own ceiling is a mildly positive combination for the pair.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the flow picture inverts on both legs. On the base leg the structural drain is measurable: the IMF's COFER data for 2026-Q2, published on 2026-09-30, show the dollar's share of allocated reserves falling to 56.70% from 57.18% while the euro's rose to 20.60%, and July TIC data show private foreigners selling $3.7bn of long-term US securities with the adjusted long-term total at -$27.9bn, the inflow carried by official buyers and Treasury bills. That is the funding profile of a currency whose holders are shortening duration. On the quote leg the constraint that caps the Singapore dollar tactically dissolves with time: at a 1.25% slope the band ceiling itself rises roughly 0.6% over six months, so today's crowding at the top resolves through the passage of time rather than through a reversal, unless MAS flattens or re-centres, which neither we nor UOB expect before 2027. Structural inflows into Singapore's wealth-management and family-office complex are a steady bid that does not reverse with sentiment, and the Q2 current-account surplus of S$37.08bn is recycled mainly through official rather than spot channels. The counterweight is the speculative dollar long, which can grow from $18.4bn toward the $30bn that would mark genuine crowding before it becomes a liability.

factors.horizon_split: The split is mechanical. Tactically the Singapore dollar is pressed against a band ceiling that MAS is actively defending with reserve accumulation while dollar longs are still building, so the pair is favoured; strategically the ceiling rises with the slope and the dollar's reserve share and private financing base erode, so the same evidence reverses sign.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Net mildly pair-positive. The base leg carries fresh, mid-range speculative length at the 44th percentile with the fastest weekly build in seven years behind it, while the quote leg has no measurable speculative position at all and is instead constrained by MAS absorbing inflows at an estimated 1.7-1.9% above the band mid-point. The pair therefore has momentum on one side and a policy cap on the other.
tactical.unwind_trigger: A soft US print — payrolls below 50,000 or core CPI at or below 0.1% month on month — or Fed speakers pushing back on a December hike, which would reverse a $12.5bn weekly dollar build as fast as it came in. On the quote side a MAS steepening to about 1.50% would release the band constraint simultaneously, so the two triggers can coincide in the last week of October.
tactical.historical_analogue: The base leg's nearest analogue is this summer: the combined cached dollar position swung $29.4bn from +$24.7bn on 2026-07-28 to -$4.7bn on 2026-08-25, a four-week reversal that moved the broad dollar roughly 2.5%. For a pair whose realised volatility is 3.15%, an equivalent squeeze is worth roughly 1-1.5%, not the 2.5% the broad index showed.
tactical.contrarian_case: The crowd is long the dollar for the first time in seven weeks and long it fast, which is the configuration that reverses on a single data point rather than decaying gracefully. Against that, the Singapore dollar's own positioning is not measurable by any speculative gauge, so what looks like crowding on the quote side is really MAS policy, and policy does not capitulate to a squeeze. The genuine contrarian risk is therefore one-sided: the pair can fall quickly on a US data miss, but it cannot rise quickly on an SGD position unwind because there is no position to unwind.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: Net mildly pair-negative. Structural reserve diversification away from the dollar continues at roughly half a percentage point of COFER share per quarter, private foreigners are net sellers of US duration, and the band ceiling that caps the Singapore dollar tactically rises about 0.6% over six months.
strategic.unwind_trigger: A speculative dollar long rebuilt beyond $30bn into the 2026-12-09 FOMC, met by a Fed that delivers its hike and then confirms a flat 2027 dot, would leave the base leg crowded into an event with no further upside; alternatively a MAS flattening or re-centring would remove the quote leg's structural bid.
strategic.historical_analogue: The same summer episode is the template at a longer remove: the dollar long peaked at +$24.7bn on 2026-07-28 and was cut to -$4.7bn within four weeks as data softened, and the broad index fell 2.5%. Over a quarter, a managed pair like this one translates that into a grind rather than a gap.
strategic.contrarian_case: The consensus contrarian case against the Singapore dollar is that it is expensive — a BIS REER of 114.81 at the 75th percentile of its post-2024 range, the second-richest in the set — and that it pays nearly 200bp of negative carry, so holders are paying to own an overvalued currency. That case has been available for two years and has lost money, because MAS sustains the richness by design rather than allowing it to correct. The honest contrarian risk to our strategic bearish call is not valuation but concentration: an AI-cycle reversal would remove the surplus, the growth and the tightening bias at once, and would do so faster than positioning data could warn.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Strategic weight raised from 0.16 to 0.18: the bilateral current-account differential is about 19.6 percentage points of GDP (Singapore +16.6%, United States -3.0%), the widest external gap in the G10+SGD set, and over one to three months it is the most durable fact about this pairing. The 0.02 comes from Factors 3 and 9. Tactical at default.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external-balance level is overwhelmingly quote-positive while the terms-of-trade direction is currently base-positive, and over four weeks the two roughly cancel. Singapore's Q2 current account was S$37.08bn, up from S$30.52bn a year earlier, with a goods surplus of S$70.39bn and a services surplus of S$14.33bn; the IMF projects 16.6% of GDP for 2026. The United States ran a Q2 current-account deficit of $246.0bn, 3.0% of GDP, with an August goods deficit of $132.6bn against a $116.3bn forecast and a net international investment position of -$22.42tn. Direct bilateral trade is small relative to both economies and close to balanced: IMF DOTS puts US goods exports to Singapore at $46.0bn and imports from Singapore at $43.2bn in 2024, a US surplus of $2.8bn, so the bilateral flow itself generates no meaningful directional pressure and the mirror statistics disagree by roughly $12bn, which is normal for an entrepot. Terms of trade is where the base leg wins: the United States is a net energy exporter and Singapore a net crude importer, and with Brent near $101-103 and WTI at $96.16, up roughly 50% on the year, the energy shock improves US terms of trade and worsens Singapore's. The offset is that Singapore's refining and shipping services surplus rises with energy volatility, and that much of the goods surplus is absorbed into MAS reserves rather than reaching spot.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.18 weight this is the factor that decides the strategic call. A current-account surplus near 16.6% of GDP against a deficit of 3.0% is not a marginal differential; it is a structural, continuing demand for the quote currency set against a continuing financing need for the base currency, and the US financing mix has deteriorated in composition as well as size. July TIC data show the inflow carried by official buyers ($44.4bn) and Treasury bills ($38.8bn) while private foreigners sold long-term securities, and the federal deficit runs near 6% of GDP alongside the external one — the twin-deficit configuration. On the quote side the goods surplus should stay elevated through the horizon with Enterprise Singapore forecasting 14-16% NODX growth for 2026, and MAS's S$550.73bn of reserves give it capacity to meter the pace in either direction. The counterweights are real but secondary. The energy terms-of-trade gain for the base leg is genuine while Brent holds near $100, but it depends on a war premium that a Gulf settlement would remove, and OCBC's framework treats $100-120 oil as inflationary rather than recessionary for Singapore. US tariff policy is a tail that could hit Singapore's exempt semiconductor and pharmaceutical categories. Netting the level differential against the terms-of-trade tilt leaves a clear Bearish direction for the pair at moderate confidence.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral tactically and Bearish strategically on the same data, because external balances move an exchange rate through cumulative financing flows that take months to bite, while the energy terms-of-trade offset that favours the base leg is strongest immediately and most vulnerable to a Gulf settlement later.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The United States is a net energy exporter: WTI at $96.16 and Henry Hub at $3.18, with crude up roughly 50% on the year. Rising oil is a terms-of-trade gain for the base leg and, through headline inflation, a reason for the Fed to stay restrictive. The dollar also carries a measured -0.53 sixty-day correlation to gold, so a gold rally is mildly base-negative.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Singapore is a net crude importer with no domestic production but is the region's largest refining and bunkering hub, so it is short crude and long refining margins and shipping activity. LNG (JKM) and crude both raise the import bill; transport inflation ran at 8.1% in August as the energy shock passed through. The framework's direction rules treat energy-importing hubs as mildly negative on an oil rise.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: the base currency gains (United States as net energy exporter, plus a hawkish Fed through headline inflation) while the quote currency loses on a higher import bill, partly offset by the refining and shipping services surplus that rises with energy volatility. Net: pair rises, but the offset is unusually large for an importer because Singapore monetises the volatility it imports. Gold up: mildly base-negative (DXY-gold correlation -0.53) and broadly neutral for Singapore, so net mildly pair-negative. Natural gas and LNG up: negative for the quote leg, mildly positive for the base leg as an LNG exporter, so net pair-positive. Iron ore and dairy are irrelevant to both legs. The dominant single driver is therefore crude, with an estimated net sensitivity that is positive for the pair but modest — perhaps a third of what the same oil move would do to a pure commodity-versus-commodity cross — because the base leg's energy export surplus is small relative to its economy and the quote leg hedges part of its import exposure through services.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from about $102 to roughly $112. Base leg gains on terms of trade and on a firmer Fed path through headline inflation; quote leg loses on a wider oil import bill and higher transport inflation, partly offset by stronger refining margins and bunkering volumes, with MAS more likely to lean hawkish on imported cost pressure. Net: pair rises, estimated 0.3-0.6%, within one or two sessions of normal range for a pair with 3.15% realised volatility. Above $130 the quote-leg damage becomes non-linear per OCBC's recessionary threshold.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent to roughly $92. Base leg loses its terms-of-trade gain and US headline inflation falls, weakening the case for a December Fed hike; quote leg gains on a lower import bill but MAS loses part of its imported-inflation justification for a steeper slope. Net: pair falls, estimated 0.3-0.5%, with the effect amplified if the fall comes from a Gulf settlement because that simultaneously removes the dollar's haven premium.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Crude oil (Brent), overwhelmingly. It is the only commodity to which both legs have material and opposing exposure, and its current level is set by the Hormuz situation rather than by demand, which makes it an event variable as much as a price variable for this pair.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks are communicating hawkishly, which is why the factor nets to nothing over four weeks even though each leg's own dossier scores it positive for its own currency. The Fed replaced conditional language on 2026-09-16 with a commitment to deliver price stability, hiked 12-0 against explicit political pressure, and published dots in which 12 of 18 participants see another 25bp by December; the Supreme Court's Trump v. Cook ruling has reduced the institutional-independence discount. Against that, Williams's remark on 2026-09-29 that there is no urgency cut October odds below a coin flip, so the near-term guidance is hawkish in level but dovish in timing. MAS has been hawkish in a different register: it raised the slope twice in 2026, the July move surprised almost everyone (only 4 of 18 analysts polled expected it), and it has said core inflation will stay elevated for several quarters. The sequence matters and is unusual here: the Fed's decision date is fixed and gated at 2026-10-28 while MAS has no schedule on file at all, with the dossiers and bank previews pointing to the last week of October. Two hawkish, credible communicators pointing in opposite currency directions in the same week is the definition of a cancelling factor.

tactical.what_is_priced: Markets price a Fed that follows its dots and a MAS tightening at roughly 45%. Both are close to our own view, so guidance offers no tactical edge on this bilateral in either direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the two guidance regimes diverge in a way that favours the quote leg, and the divergence is about shape rather than hawkishness. The Fed's guidance is explicitly a plateau: the SEP median is 4.1% for both 2026 and 2027 and 3.9% for 2028, which tells the market the base leg's policy support stops extending after at most one more move at the 2026-12-09 SEP meeting. MAS's guidance is explicitly one-way: it has said core inflation will moderate discernibly only from around mid-2027, which rules out an easing inside our horizon, and its instrument appreciates continuously at the band slope rather than sitting still between decisions. A plateauing rate against a continuously appreciating band is, mechanically, a narrowing differential even with no decision taken by either side. Credibility is high on both legs and that matters asymmetrically: the Fed's credibility keeps breakevens anchored at 2.36% despite 3.4% headline PCE and prevents the US fiscal position from becoming a currency crisis, which is a genuine offset; but MAS's credibility means the band's appreciation actually gets delivered, which a rate-setting central bank cannot promise. The political tail on the base leg — renewed pressure on Fed independence — accumulates with time and has no counterpart on the quote leg.

The asymmetry it underprices is that a plateau is a decision to stop while an appreciating band is a decision that keeps executing, so the differential narrows without either committee doing anything.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk for this pair is dense and genuinely two-sided inside four weeks. The dominant geopolitical driver is the seven-month US-Iran war: Hormuz crude flows have recovered to 9.719 mb/d, about 80% of pre-war levels, the US maintains a naval blockade and has signalled it may resume strikes, and Trump rejected Iran's seven-day reopening roadmap while calling the indirect talks productive. A renewed Hormuz disruption is unambiguously pair-positive — it lifts the dollar on haven demand and raises Singapore's import bill simultaneously, hitting both legs in the same direction — while a settlement is pair-negative for the same reason in reverse. Those are the only two events that move both legs at once, which is what makes them matter disproportionately for this bilateral rather than for either currency alone. The scheduled cluster is concentrated: MAS's statement is expected in the last week of October though no SGD schedule exists in the gated file, the FOMC is fixed at 2026-10-28, and the US midterms fall on 2026-11-03 just outside the window but inside a one-month option tenor. Bilateral political risk is modest: the 12.5% US tariff on about S$9.5bn of Singapore exports since 24 July exempts semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and energy, so it spares the sectors driving the boom. Probabilities on the two dominant tails are close enough that the factor nets to zero.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the event map broadens and the skew remains close to flat because the base-leg and quote-leg risks pull in opposite directions. Against the dollar: the 2026-11-03 midterms determine control of Congress heading into the continuing resolution's expiry on 2026-12-11, with a shutdown probability around 35%, and Fitch flagged gridlock and shutdown risk when it affirmed AA+ in August. A Gulf settlement, more likely over a quarter than over a month at roughly 25%, would remove the energy premium supporting US terms of trade and the dollar's haven bid. Against the Singapore dollar: renewed escalation at roughly 20% would hit an energy-importing trade hub hardest, and the exemption of semiconductors and pharmaceuticals from US tariffs is a policy choice that can be revoked, which would strike precisely the sectors behind the 2026 growth surprise. A China-Taiwan escalation is a low-probability, high-impact event that disrupts Singapore's trade routes while initially attracting regional haven flows, so even its sign is ambiguous for this pair. Three meaningful dollar-negative events against two meaningful Singapore-dollar-negative events, with the latter carrying larger per-event magnitude, nets to Neutral rather than to a direction.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral at both horizons with identical confidence. The composition changes — tactically the Gulf binary dominates, strategically the US fiscal calendar and the tariff-exemption risk join it — but the offsetting structure does not, because almost every event that hurts one leg helps the other.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign differential on this pair is as wide as any in the G10+SGD set, and over four weeks it does not matter. Singapore is rated AAA with a stable outlook, affirmed by Fitch on 2026-04-02, runs a projected FY2026 budget surplus of S$8.5bn (1.0% of GDP) after a revised FY2025 surplus of 1.9%, issues debt to develop its bond market rather than to fund deficits, and holds a strongly positive net asset position backed by S$550.73bn of official reserves. The United States is rated one notch below AAA at all three agencies, runs a deficit near 6% of GDP with debt held by the public at 101% and net interest above $1.0tn, now larger than defence spending. Yet the transmission over four weeks runs the wrong way for the obvious conclusion: the base leg's fiscal deterioration shows up as a higher term premium, and a 5.24% 10-year has been attracting capital rather than repelling it, with $83.7bn of July TIC inflows. Singapore's 24 September 6-month auction cleared S$8.4bn at 1.92% with 1.88 times cover, and no fiscal event falls on either leg inside the window — the US funding deadline is 2026-12-11 and Singapore's Budget 2027 is in February. The differential is a background constant, not a tactical driver.

tactical.what_is_priced: SGS yielding 275bp through Treasuries already prices Singapore's AAA status and reserve backing, and the base leg's fiscal risk is priced in the term premium rather than in the currency. Neither repricing is due inside four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the mechanism by which the sovereign gap reaches the exchange rate starts to operate. US net interest above 3.3% of GDP compounds against a deficit the CBO puts at 5.8% before the recent rise in yields, with debt held by the public projected to run from 101% toward 120% by 2036, and the tariff revenue that was supposed to offset part of it is shrinking after the IEEPA ruling and the expiry of the Section 122 levies. A 10-year at 5.24% against a longer-run dot of 3.2% implies roughly 100bp or more of term premium: the bond market is already charging for supply. The link that has protected the dollar — higher yields pulling in capital — weakens precisely as peers' yields rise, and the 2026-12-11 funding deadline with a roughly 35% shutdown probability is the event that could transfer the premium from the curve to the currency. Singapore has the opposite problem, which is to say none: fiscal policy is constitutionally rule-bound, revenue is likely to overshoot the budget framed on a 2.0-4.0% growth assumption now that growth is 4.5-5.5%, and rating action is implausible. Fiscal strength also lets MAS run the band for inflation rather than for growth, which is the indirect channel by which it supports the quote leg. The gap is the widest on the pair and it finally points somewhere over this horizon.

We expect that link to weaken as peer yields rise, at which point the premium shows up as currency weakness rather than only as a steeper curve.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral tactically and Bearish strategically on an unchanged differential, because over four weeks the base leg's fiscal deterioration manifests as higher yields that attract capital and support the pair, while over a quarter the interest burden, shrinking tariff revenue and the December funding cliff transfer the risk from the curve to the currency.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Tactical lowered from 0.05 to 0.03 and strategic from 0.03 to 0.02: no exchange lists an SGD option, so implied volatility, the IV percentile, risk reversals, the term structure and the variance risk premium are permanently unobservable for every SGD pair. Roughly half this factor's prescribed inputs do not exist, and it should not carry full weight on half its evidence. The tactical 0.02 moves to Factor 1; the strategic 0.01 moves to Factor 5.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the one factor where the pair's own trading behaviour is the legitimate subject, and what it says is that the pair does not trend. Realised volatility is about 3.19% on 20 days and 3.15% on 60 days, the lowest of any major pairing in the set and roughly half AUD/USD's, which is exactly what a managed float against a band produces. Implied volatility is not merely missing but permanently absent: no exchange lists an SGD option, so there is no 1-month or 3-month implied, no IV percentile, no 25-delta risk reversal and no term structure to read event pricing from, and pair_3m_iv is therefore null with a null source rather than an estimate. The same applies to the forward funding differential: SGD has no listed future, so the direction payload returns funding unavailable and the forward points quoted anywhere on this pair are CIP constructions, not market observations. The store's own quality note records that only seven resistance and one support zone met the two-touch threshold, which is itself a structural statement — a managed pair generates few durable clustered swing closes because the policy band suppresses the excursions that create them. Neither a trend regime nor a volatility regime gives this pair a tactical direction, and placing levels is pass two's work with data this pass does not hold.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the structural picture is unchanged in kind: a low-volatility managed market in which direction is delivered slowly rather than in breaks. At roughly 3.15% annualised realised volatility, a 1.5% move takes about a quarter to accumulate in a normal regime, which means a correct strategic view on this pair is paid in time rather than in size and that stop-based expressions are poorly suited to it. There is no vol surface to tell us whether the market is pricing a regime change, no skew to tell us which side dealers are hedging, and no term structure to tell us how the December event cluster is being priced — all three are permanently unavailable. The one genuinely structural observation is that the absence of an options market removes the hedging channel through which other pairs amplify directional moves, which is part of why this pair's distribution is so tight. The framework's minimum of three resistance and three support zones cannot be satisfied from this pass's payload in any case, since zones were deliberately removed; the store note that only one support zone cleared the two-touch threshold is recorded for pass two. Neutral is the only defensible stance.

expression_assessment.vol_landscape_summary: The pair's realised volatility is about 3.15-3.19% annualised, the lowest major pairing in the set, and there is no implied volatility at all because no exchange lists an SGD option — this is a permanent feature of the market, not a data gap. Consequently the variance risk premium, the skew and the event premium around the October and December decision cluster are all unmeasurable. The vol landscape is therefore defined by one fact: this is a managed, slow, tight-distribution market in which directional conviction is expressed through time and size rather than through convexity.
expression_assessment.directional_expression: Spot and forwards are the only available instruments. strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the Fed's operating framework works against the base leg of this pair. Reserve management purchases of roughly $10bn a month and the rollover of all Treasury principal grow the balance sheet slowly — total assets are $155.9bn higher than a year ago — and the standing repo facility at 4.00% caps any funding spike, which removes the mechanism by which reserve scarcity has supported the dollar in past tightening cycles. The Desk is instructed to buy bills as needed to keep reserves ample, so the structural drain that accompanied earlier cycles simply does not exist. At the same time, hiking by the Fed's peers lowers the cost of hedging dollar assets for foreign holders and encourages higher hedge ratios, which is dollar selling forward. On the quote side the picture is the mirror image: Singapore's role as the Asian dollar hub means the easing of dollar funding pressure feeds quickly into local rates and forwards, and MAS's S$550.73bn of reserves make a disorderly Singapore dollar funding squeeze essentially impossible. The counter-risk, and the reason confidence is only 52, is the year-end turn: the 2026-12-11 funding deadline and a possible Treasury General Account distortion could tighten conditions for two or three weeks and briefly lift the pair, with reserves at $2.948tn already near the roughly $3tn comfort benchmark.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.3540 is clearly Bearish USD/SGD, and here the breadth is genuine rather than cosmetic: six of ten factors are Bearish, four are Neutral, and not one is Bullish. The largest single contribution is External Balance at -0.1026, followed by Guidance at -0.0648, USD Liquidity at -0.0624, Inflation & Growth at -0.0550, Fiscal at -0.0392 and Flows at -0.0300. What restrains the score from going further is that the heaviest factor, Policy & Rates at 0.24, contributes exactly nothing — the carry gap that would resist a falling pair is almost perfectly offset by a forward curve that already discounts it. That is the key structural feature of this call: the direction is well-supported by breadth, but the single largest weight is silent, no individual factor exceeds 57% confidence, and the pair's 3.15% realised volatility means the view is paid slowly. A score of this size on six low-confidence factors is a conviction-3 reading, not a conviction-4 one.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the four heaviest factors — Policy & Rates at 0.24, External Balance at 0.18, Guidance at 0.12 and USD Liquidity at 0.12 — carry 66% of the decision, and three of them point the same way. External Balance dominates with -0.1026: a Singapore current-account surplus near 16.6% of GDP against a US deficit of 3.0%, a gap of about 19.6 percentage points, is the widest external differential in the set, and the US side is financed increasingly by official buyers and Treasury bills while private foreigners sell duration. Guidance adds -0.0648 because the two communication regimes have different shapes rather than different levels: the Fed's SEP is an explicit plateau at 4.1% through 2027, while MAS has ruled out easing before mid-2027 and runs an instrument that appreciates continuously at about 1.25% a year, so the differential narrows without either committee acting. USD Liquidity adds -0.0624 because the ample-reserve framework and the 4.00% standing repo cap remove the funding-scarcity channel that has supported the dollar in past cycles, while peer hikes lower foreign hedging costs. Fiscal adds -0.0392 on the widest sovereign gap on the pair — AAA with a surplus against AA+ with a 6%-of-GDP deficit and net interest above $1tn. Policy & Rates, the heaviest factor, is silent: the 195.5bp carry is real but the CIP-derived forward already discounts 1.96% a year, more than the band slope delivers, so a short-pair position must beat the forward rather than spot. The two dossiers reinforce rather than conflict here — the dollar ranks 8th of 11 strategically at -0.1822, the Singapore dollar 4th at +0.2160 — and the bilateral-specific modifiers all push the same way: MAS absorbs the surplus but the band ceiling rises 0.6% over six months, releasing the tactical cap, and Singapore's role as the Asian dollar hub means easing dollar funding transmits quickly. What is priced is a stable band and a plateauing Fed; what is not priced is a Fed pause coinciding with an unchanged or steeper MAS slope. The decisive dates are the 2026-12-09 FOMC with its SEP, the 2026-12-11 funding deadline and the January 2027 MAS statement. Conviction is 3 rather than 4 because no factor exceeds 57% confidence, because the whole thesis rests on one concentrated AI export cycle that could turn within two quarters, and because the carry runs against the position throughout.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge by a full stance and the divergence is mechanical rather than a judgement call. Three specific factors flip sign between them. Flows & Positioning is Bullish tactically because the S$NEER sits an estimated 1.7-1.9% above its band mid-point with almost no headroom while dollar longs are still building, and Bearish strategically because the band ceiling rises about 0.6% at the 1.25% slope, releasing exactly that constraint. USD Liquidity is Neutral tactically because October funding is calm, and Bearish strategically because the ample-reserve framework and peer hikes add dollar supply over a quarter. Fiscal is Neutral tactically because a 5.24% 10-year attracts capital, and Bearish strategically because the December funding cliff and the interest burden transfer the premium from the curve to the currency. On top of the sign flips, the weight shift does independent work: External Balance moves from 0.06 to 0.18 and Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12, so two factors that are Bearish at both horizons contribute almost nothing tactically and -0.1674 strategically.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The last week of October, when the FOMC on 2026-10-28 and the MAS statement expected in that week resolve together, with a second and larger checkpoint at the 2026-12-09 FOMC, which is the only projection round in the gated calendar and the decision that either delivers the Fed's last hike or prices it out. Pass-2 timing: MAS now reports no later than 2026-10-14 [40], alongside US CPI the same day, and the FOMC follows on 2026-10-28.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the tactical and strategic views as sequential rather than contradictory: the carry-positive tactical position is a four-week proposition that should be reassessed, not rolled, after the October decision cluster, and the strategic short should be built after that cluster rather than before it, when the base leg's rate momentum has been either confirmed or exhausted. Because the pair has no listed options, the switch has to be managed by sizing and timing in linear instruments. Note also that the strategic position pays roughly 195.5bp a year in negative carry while the tactical one collects it, so holding period discipline matters more on this pair than on most. In price terms, the switch from tactical long to strategic short happens in the 1.2812–1.2876 lower half of the seven-touch resistance band, after the FOMC; if MAS steepens and the pair closes below 1.2740 before that, the tactical leg is stopped and the strategic short can be entered early on a retest of 1.2780–1.2800.

forward_vs_spot.edge_3m: −11 pips (probability-weighted): broadly in line with the forward; this is where the tactical-to-strategic switch happens (1M edge is +48 pips pair-positive probability-weighted, +78 base case)
forward_vs_spot.edge_6m: −68 pips pair-negative (base case); only −15 pips probability-weighted. Forwards are CIP constructions (SOFR 3.88% vs 1.92% T-bill) and differ from tradeable forwards by the unobservable cross-currency basis; on a SORA basis the 6-month outright would be closer to 1.2610, which would remove most of the strategic edge. The strategic short is only worth running from a better entry (about 1.2840), not from spot.

catalysts.event: FOMC minutes of the 15-16 September meeting
catalysts.rationale: The minutes reveal how broad the hawkish majority was behind a 12-0 hike in which 12 of 18 dots show another move this year. A broad majority lifts December odds and front-end yields, widening the pair's roughly 195.5bp short-rate gap at the margin. There is no quote-leg equivalent, because MAS publishes no vote and no minutes, so this is a one-sided event that acts directly on the pair's carry.

catalysts.event: MAS Monetary Policy Statement and Macroeconomic Review (no later than 2026-10-14; pass-2 date correction from 2026-10-W4 per MAS Advance Release Calendar)
catalysts.rationale: This is the largest single quote-leg event in both horizons and the one factor capable of overturning the tactical call inside the window. Our probabilities are 40% for a steepening to about 1.50%, 58% for an unchanged slope at about 1.25% and 2% for easing, against a survey at 45% for tightening; CIMB expects the steepening, UOB a hold. A steepening lifts the S$NEER an estimated 0.2-0.4% on the day and is pair-negative; even a hold leaves the band appreciating, so the expected impact skews negative for the pair. Pass-2 addition: OCBC and Standard Chartered have since joined CIMB in calling a slight steepening [41][42], so the bank count now leans toward tightening.

August headline was 3.4% with core at 2.4%, and gasoline accounted for over a third of the monthly rise. A core print at or above 0.3% month on month keeps the December hike live and sustains the pair's carry; 0.1% or below would knock December odds below 50% and remove the tactical case. The asymmetry matters more here than on most pairs because the quote leg has no rate that can respond. Pass-2 addition: this may fall on the same day as the MAS statement. A soft CPI combined with a MAS steepening is the cluster most likely to produce the tactical downside case.

catalysts.event: Singapore Q3 2026 advance GDP estimate (MTI) — source date given in week-format 2026-10-W2; historically released alongside the MAS statement
catalysts.rationale: The MAS survey expects 4.6% year on year while non-oil exports and the PMI point to 5% or more. A print above 5% raises the odds of a third slope steepening at the October statement, which is the only mechanism by which Singapore growth reaches the exchange rate; below 4% it removes that case and the pair's main quote-leg risk with it.

catalysts.event: Singapore September non-oil domestic exports (Enterprise Singapore) — source date given in week-format 2026-10-W3
catalysts.rationale: August NODX rose 46.2% year on year with electronics up 131.8%, the fastest since 1988. Continued strength sustains the goods surplus that underpins the strategic bearish case for the pair and strengthens the tightening argument; a drop below 15% would be the first evidence that the AI cycle is fading, which is the single largest risk to the strategic call.

catalysts.event: Singapore September CPI and MAS core inflation (pass-2 date correction from 2026-10-W4 per MAS calendar; after the policy statement)
catalysts.rationale: Core was 2.2% in August, a two-year high and in the upper half of MAS's 1.5-2.5% range, against a survey full-year median of only 1.9%. A print at 2.3% or higher ahead of the policy statement makes the tightening case difficult to dismiss and is pair-negative; a fall toward 1.6% would validate UOB's hold call and relieve the quote leg. Pass-2 note: because the print now follows the statement, it matters mainly for the January 2027 MAS statement and so for the strategic view.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision, no Summary of Economic Projections (gated calendar, firm)
catalysts.rationale: Our base case is a hawkish hold at 3.75-4.00% with December kept live, which sustains the pair's carry; a hike at roughly 35% probability would be clearly pair-positive and a dovish hold pair-negative. Its proximity to the expected MAS statement means the two legs resolve within days of each other, so the week's net effect on the pair depends on which surprises more, not on either in isolation.

Control of Congress determines the path to the 2026-12-11 funding deadline and fiscal policy into 2027. A divided result raises shutdown risk and revives the governance concerns Fitch flagged at its AA+ affirmation; a unified result raises fiscal-expansion risk and the term premium. Both routes are base-negative over a quarter, and there is no quote-leg counterpart because Singapore's politics are stable and its fiscal rules constitutional.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections (gated calendar, firm, SEP)
catalysts.rationale: This is the decision that defines the base leg's plateau and it is the only projection round in the gated window. A delivered hike with an unchanged 4.1% dot for 2027 marks the end of the dollar's rate momentum against a quote currency whose band keeps appreciating, which is the pivot our strategic case rests on. A 2027 dot raised to 4.4% would invalidate it and restore the pair's rate support.

catalysts.event: Expiry of the continuing resolution — US government funding deadline
catalysts.rationale: A shutdown, which the base dossier puts at roughly 35%, would revive governance concerns and is base-negative for the currency, pulling the pair lower. But it lands in the year-end funding turn and could distort the Treasury General Account, tightening dollar funding and briefly pushing the dollar to the left of its smile, which is pair-positive. Singapore's position as the Asian dollar hub means that funding channel reaches the quote leg's rates within days, amplifying the second effect on this pair specifically.

catalysts.event: Year-end US dollar funding window — recurring seasonal (source date given in week-format 2026-12-W4)
catalysts.rationale: September quarter-end showed the mechanism on this pair: SOFR firmed toward 3.90% and Singapore's 6-month T-bill repriced 22bp in a fortnight. A similar year-end squeeze lifts the pair temporarily through both legs at once — dollar funding demand on one side, Asian dollar-market transmission on the other — and is the main timing risk to a strategic short held through December rather than entered after it.

catalysts.event: MAS Monetary Policy Statement, January 2027 — source date given in week-format 2027-01-W4, outside the four-month gated window
catalysts.rationale: Nearly all survey respondents expect no change, and a hold at a 1.25-1.50% slope confirms that the band keeps appreciating through the first quarter, which is the quote-leg assumption underpinning the strategic bearish view. UOB frames a slight steepening at this meeting as its risk case. A flattening would be the clean invalidation of the strategic call but carries a probability below 10%.

invalidators.mechanism: The policy cap that makes SGD-positive news 'absorbed rather than expressed' would be shown to be released inside the window, removing the Flows support (+0.0530) that tips the tactical score over +0.10.

invalidators.condition: US September core CPI (2026-10-14) prints 0.1% m/m or lower AND December hike odds fall below 40%
invalidators.mechanism: The carry leg would remain but its rate momentum would vanish, and the $18.4bn speculative dollar long, built in a week, would unwind faster in this low-vol pair than the carry accrues (roughly 21 pips a month against a 1–1.5% squeeze).
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Core CPI m/m; fed funds futures

invalidators.mechanism: The proxy gap would widen back toward 220bp instead of narrowing to about 170bp, undoing the 'plateau versus appreciating band' logic behind Guidance (−0.0648) and making the short pay more carry over a longer horizon.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SEP; T-bill auction cut-offs; USD/SGD weekly close

invalidators.mechanism: Growth (−0.0550), the external surplus (−0.1026) and MAS's tightening bias would go together, and none of those losses would come from the dollar side.

invalidators.mechanism: This is the only shock that hurts SGD (crossing OCBC's recessionary threshold for Singapore) and helps USD (energy exporter and haven) at the same moment, turning the net commodity exposure from modest to dominant.

invalidators.mechanism: The band's continuous appreciation is the mechanism behind the narrowing differential in Factors 1 and 6, and without it the 195.5bp carry dominates.

invalidators.new_stance: Neutral (strategic short on hold, re-entry only after the turn)
invalidators.mechanism: Singapore's Asian-dollar-hub role transmits a US funding squeeze into SGD rates and forwards within days, lifting the pair through both legs at once.

signposts.indicator: UOB S$NEER model, distance above band mid-point
signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: stays at 1.6% or more after a MAS hold (ceiling still binding). Strategic: holds 1.5–2.0% after a steepening (band delivers the faster slope).
signposts.invalidates_if: Falls below 1.0% above mid (MAS easing bias, or SGD demand fading)
signposts.bilateral_importance: For this pair the S$NEER position is the only observable measure of SGD 'positioning', since there is no CFTC contract and no options. It decides whether Singapore's strong data reach USD/SGD at all.

signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: stays at or below 1.95% (gap of 195bp or more). Strategic: rises to 2.10–2.20% (gap narrows to about 170bp).
signposts.invalidates_if: Falls below 1.60% (tactical carry widens and the strategic narrowing fails)
signposts.bilateral_importance: It is the quote leg of the only usable rate differential. Singapore has no policy rate, so this yield alone sets the carry and the CIP forward on this pair.

signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: daily close above 1.2835. Strategic: weekly close below 1.2740 after the October FOMC, then below 1.2628.
signposts.invalidates_if: Tactical: daily close below 1.2715. Strategic: weekly close above 1.2976.
signposts.bilateral_importance: 1.2740 is the top of the only computed support (6 touches) and 1.2976 the bottom of the 3-touch zone above the 7-touch band. In a 3% vol pair these bands mark where the policy band and the dollar have historically traded off.

signposts.indicator: US 2-year Treasury minus effective fed funds
signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: holds above +75bp into 2026-10-28. Strategic: compresses below +50bp after 2026-12-09 (plateau priced).
signposts.invalidates_if: Tactical: falls below +50bp before 2026-10-28. Strategic: rises above +110bp after the December SEP.
signposts.bilateral_importance: The quote leg has no rate to respond, so the base leg's front end alone drives changes in this pair's differential.

signposts.indicator: MAS core inflation, year on year
signposts.confirms_if: Strategic: 2.3% or higher in the 2026-10-23 or November prints, which sets up a January 2027 steepening
signposts.invalidates_if: 1.6% or lower (opens a flattening debate and removes the strategic quote-leg driver)
signposts.bilateral_importance: It is the input that decides whether MAS steepens the slope. On this pair, Singapore inflation reaches the exchange rate only through the band, with no rate channel to dilute it.

signposts.indicator: Reuters Asian FX positioning poll — USD/SGD score
signposts.current_level: Modest SGD longs, 'consistent since early August' [45]
signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: SGD longs pared further before 2026-10-14. Strategic: SGD longs rebuilt after a MAS steepening while USD/SGD holds below 1.2800.
signposts.invalidates_if: Tactical: SGD longs jump to multi-month highs before the statement (market front-running a steepening)
signposts.bilateral_importance: It is the only NDF-inclusive speculative positioning gauge for the quote leg. Combined with the IMM dollar long, it gives a two-sided view of pair crowding.

signposts.invalidates_if: A monthly fall of more than S$5bn (MAS defending the weak side, so the band is no longer a cap on SGD)
signposts.bilateral_importance: Reserve accumulation is how Singapore's 16.6%-of-GDP surplus is kept out of USD/SGD spot. A change in its pace changes how much of the external gap reaches the pair.

assumptions: Price series as delivered (verbatim from the payload): dataPoints 130; dateRange 2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02; spot 1.2793; spotDate 2026-10-02; computationRange 2007-12-21 to 2026-10-02 (4901 weekday bars); dataBasis weekday (Mon-Fri) bars from the gated append-only store, SMAs are simple averages of trading-day closes, realised vol annualised on 252; weekendBarsDropped 0.

Payload dataQuality: 'USD/SGD: only 7 resistance / 1 support zones met the 2-touch threshold — supplement with round numbers and note the shortfall'; 'USD/SGD: 4901 weekday bars in the store (2007-12-21 to 2026-10-02); 1007 weekly, 462 monthly; 130 daily bars passed downstream (2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02), which is the 1-6 month strategic horizon'.

Spot-date gap: spotDate (2026-10-02) is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date, when the pair closed at 1.2805. Every level, pip distance, percentage, MA distance, scenario target and forward outright is anchored to the payload spot of 1.2793. No web quote was substituted.

Support shortfall: only one support zone met the two-touch threshold, so the support list is supplemented with the round number 1.2700, the 52-week closing low (1.26139), the 52-week intraday low (1.25883) and the psychological 1.2500, each labelled as a supplement. Zone distances are to zone midpoints as supplied in the payload.

Settled verdict: all ten factors and the synthesis (stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, contributions, net scores, convictions, interpretations, rationales, rankings, consensus and cross-horizon blocks) are carried verbatim from pass 1. Additions are labelled Pass-2 note, Pass-2 technical supplement or Pass-2 addendum, and none changes a score. The publishable disagreement is that the tactical Bullish call is more fragile than its +0.1024 suggests: the MAS statement is now dated no later than 2026-10-14 and three of four tracked bank previews expect a steepening.

Calendar corrections (outside the scored block): the MAS Advance Release Calendar [40] gives the October MPS and Macroeconomic Review as 'NLT 14 Oct 2026', September CPI on 23 Oct 2026, and MAS assets and liabilities (reserves) data on 14 Oct 2026. These replace pass 1's week-format, unconfirmed Singapore dates in the catalyst list only.

Catalyst date formatting: the source gives some catalysts in week format (2026-10-W2, 2026-10-W3, 2026-12-W4, 2027-01-W4). To meet the YYYY-MM-DD schema these were converted to approximate calendar dates (2026-10-14, 2026-10-17, 2026-12-28, 2027-01-25); the original week-format is preserved in each event string. 'Mostly priced' for the January 2027 MAS catalyst is mapped to 'Partially'.

Rates: there is no SGD policy rate. Carry uses the 6-month SGS T-bill (1.92%) against the Fed's 3.875% effective midpoint, giving +195.5bp; on 3-month compounded SORA it would be about 281bp. The payload USD 10-year (4.68%) is a monthly 2026-08-01 vintage and is not used as a live level.

Volatility and forwards: implied volatility, risk reversals and the vol term structure do not exist for any SGD pair. pair_3m_iv is null and was neither estimated nor searched for; the corresponding implied-vol fields in market_context are null for the same reason, and quote_cftc_percentile 0 is a placeholder (no CFTC contract for SGD). The carry-to-vol figure is shown only on realised vol and labelled as a proxy. Realised vol is cited as 2.94% (20d) / 3.17% (60d) in the Market Context section and about 3.19% / 3.15% in the factor text; rv_1m uses the Market Context figure. Forward points are CIP-derived (SOFR 3.88% vs 1.92%, actual/365) because SGD has no listed future, and differ from tradeable forwards by the unobservable cross-currency basis.
Position sizing convention: risk 0.25% of NAV at conviction 2 and 0.5% at conviction 3. Stops are placed in ATR units (ATR(14) = 39 pips) beyond computed zones, not inside them.

Pass-1 assumptions carried forward: bilateral trade is taken directly from the supplied IMF DOTS block. The mirror statistics disagree (US-reported imports from Singapore $43.2bn vs Singapore-reported exports $44.1bn; US-reported exports $46.0bn vs Singapore-reported imports $55.9bn), so the $2.8bn net is approximate. S$NEER band parameters are bank estimates; the newest numeric reading used is UOB's 1.76% above mid (2026-09-25). The USD/SGD cross-currency basis is not observable from free sources. Retail extrapolation forecast sites seen in search were excluded.

In the strategic scenarios the source labels the SGD-stronger case (1.2450) 'Upside' and the USD-stronger case (1.2960) 'Downside', reflecting the Bearish strategic stance; they are mapped as labelled.
